id.description: Permanent id: state key, route namespace (`/api/x/<id>/`), log prefix. Never rename.

hostApiVersion.description: Integer, equal to the host's HOST_API_VERSION.

frontend.description: Frontend ESM entry; omitted by a plugin that contributes no UI.

sidecar.description: Image + health path, expected when `kind: "sidecar"`. Not enforced at load (#784): without it the health poll uses `/healthz`. Every bundled sidecar plugin's is checked in CI.

capabilities.description: Host-agent capabilities the plugin may use, each granted per machine in Admin (E4). A job's own `capabilities` (#843) is a subset of this list.

AcPluginManifest.description: The `acPlugin` block of a plugin's package.json — everything the host needs before it loads any code. The host validates this against the generated JSON Schema (issue #26). `hostApiVersion` is an integer that must equal the host's `HOST_API_VERSION`.

PluginKind.description: How the host runs a plugin.

SidecarSpec.description: A sidecar plugin's image and health path, expected when `kind === "sidecar"`. The host reads only `healthPath` (its health poll) and never `image` (the compose file names the sidecar's image).

attention.description: #78: the plugin serves `GET /api/x/<id>/attention` -> `{ ok: true, items: AttentionItem[] }` (`attention.ts`). The `overview` plugin's rollup card discovers contributors via `PluginView.attention` (`views.ts`) rather than a second manifest read. Additive; always `true` when present (a boolean, not a route list, since the path is fixed). The plugin must also declare that route in `routes` and register it; the host checks neither at load (#784; every bundled plugin's is checked in CI), and the rollup counts a contributor whose route fails as not loaded.

Contributes.description: The contribution points a plugin offers. Every field is optional; a plugin contributes a subset.

route.description: Route the panel mounts at, e.g. "/board".

nav.description: Named nav slot this panel wants to own (e.g. "issues"); optional.

order.description: Where this panel wants to sit among the tabs (#472): a finite number, lower first, after the fixed `Home` tab. Unset keeps the panel after every ordered one, in the existing order (plugin directory name, then declaration order), so declaring `order` on one panel never moves a panel that did not. A hint, not a claim: the operator's `tab_order` setting outranks it, and among the ordered panels an `installed` plugin's never precedes a `bundled` plugin's, so a third-party package declaring a small number cannot jump ahead of the bundled ordered panels (it still precedes every panel that declares no `order`). Additive; a manifest without it validates as before.

export.description: The export name in the plugin's frontend bundle.

isolation.description: Reserved (design §4, #124): `"iframe"` asks the host to mount this panel in an iframe. Not implemented in 2.0; the host accepts and ignores it, so a panel declaring it still loads in-process.

export.description: The export name in the plugin's frontend bundle.

title.description: Button/label text; the shell falls back to `id` when omitted.

scope.description: What the action operates on, e.g. "issue" | "report" | "global".

confirm.description: Accepted, but inert since #530: the modal is the one confirmation, so neither it nor the palette asks for a second click.

fields.description: The form the shell builds the action's modal from; omit for a no-input action.

ActionContribution.description: An action; the shell builds its button + modal from these fields (#34), and opening the modal is the action's one confirmation (#530).

name.description: Key the submitted value is collected under.

options.description: Choices for a `select`. A bare string is both value and label; the object form allows a distinct display label (so a later value≠label select is additive, not a breaking `string[]`→object change).

optionsFrom.description: Choices fetched from a plugin route instead (#463), for a `select` or `multiselect` only -- the validator rejects it on any other type, and beside a non-empty `options` (one source of choices, not two). When the route cannot be loaded the shell degrades the field to a text box (a `multiselect`'s text is a comma-separated list) and shows the reason, so an action is never blocked by its picker. Additive.

ActionField.description: One field of an action's form; the shell builds a labelled control from it.

ActionFieldType.description: Input control kind for an action field; the shell renders each `fields` entry by its `type`. `multiselect` (#463) is a set of choices whose submitted value is a `string[]`; `hidden` (#463) is a value with no control at all -- a snapshot the operator must not type into (the seed, the stored draft or the default is submitted unchanged). Both are additive; every earlier type behaves as before.

route.description: The route, relative to the declaring plugin's own namespace: the shell fetches `/api/x/<plugin-id><route>`. It must start with `/`, carry no query string, fragment, `..`, `//`, `%` or `\`, and be one of the plugin's own declared `GET` routes (`contributes.routes`).

params.description: Names of OTHER fields of the same action whose current values are sent as query parameters (so a route can answer for the repo the operator has typed, say). The route is not fetched while any of them is empty, and is fetched again when one changes.

ActionOptionsSource.description: Where a `select` / `multiselect` field's choices come from when they are not a fixed `options` list (#463): a `GET` route the DECLARING plugin itself registers, answering an `ActionOptionsResponse` (`action-options.ts`). The host validates it at manifest-load time (`plugins/validate.ts`).

schedule.description: 5-field cron expression (the host's `jobs/cron.ts` grammar). Not validated when the plugin loads (#784): a schedule that does not parse is logged at warn when the scheduler starts and the job is never scheduled, while the plugin itself loads as usual. Every bundled plugin's schedules are parsed in CI.

timeoutSec.description: Per-run timeout in seconds. Must be at least 1: a zero or negative value would fire the timeout at once, timing out any run that awaits real I/O (#137). And at most 2147483, about 24.8 days: Node clamps a longer or non-finite `setTimeout` delay to 1 ms, which fires it at once, the same failure (#580).

minAgentVersion.description: A `runOn: "agent"` job is not dispatched to a machine whose paired agent version compares lower than this (#372, #80); the run row records the skip with its reason instead. Ignored for a `runOn: "host"` job. Additive; absent means every paired machine is always dispatched, as before this field existed.

capabilities.description: The host-agent capabilities this job's verbs need on a machine (#843). A `runOn: "agent"` job is not dispatched to a paired machine that has not granted this plugin every one of them. That machine's row records `skipped` with reason `not granted: <capability>[, ...]` instead: no run is recorded, no `job.finished` is emitted and no failure is notified. Each must be declared in the plugin's top-level `capabilities` (the host refuses the manifest otherwise). Ignored for a `runOn: "host"` job. Additive: absent or empty dispatches to every paired machine, as before this field existed. A host released before this field refuses a manifest that declares it.

JobRunOn.description: Where a contributed job runs: in the host, or fanned out to the paired agents (E4).

path.description: Path under the plugin's namespace, e.g. "/feed".

RouteContribution.description: An HTTP route; the host mounts it under `/api/x/<plugin-id>/<path>`.

HttpMethod.description: HTTP method for a contributed route.

SettingType.description: JSON scalar type of a plugin setting (rendered by Admin).

ThemeContribution.description: A theme contributed as token JSON only (no code).

slot.description: The slot name, one of the `SLOTS` ids, e.g. "issues".

version.description: Integer slot version; the host resolves provider/consumer by exact equality.

SlotRef.description: A named, versioned slot this plugin provides or consumes.

format.description: Anchored regex the value is expected to match, e.g. "^[0-9]+$". Not enforced by the host; every bundled plugin's compiles and is anchored (checked in CI).

required.description: Whether the plugin needs a value. Not enforced by the host: a missing value reads `undefined`.

EnvVar.description: A declared environment variable (field names shared verbatim with the discord-bot index). Declaring a key is what lets `HostApi.env.get` read it. `format` and `required` are metadata only: the host checks a value against neither (#784), so a plugin that depends on one checks its own value.
